npcs.name: Armand Christophe
npcs.greet: Easy, friend. On the Waterfront, a man who asks too many questions gets answers from the lake. Ask me the right one.

npcs.name: S'krivva
npcs.greet: This one keeps the Guild's business in Bravil. Speak softly. The walls here are thin and the guards are thick.

npcs.name: The Gray Fox
npcs.greet: You'll forget my face the moment you look away. Don't take it personally. It's an old trick, and not one I chose.

npcs.name: Millona Umbranox
npcs.greet: Anvil has had a countess and no count for a very long time. I have grown used to answering for both.

relics.name: Magistrate's Signet
relics.desc: A Bravil magistrate's seal ring, heavy gold. Its owner will be very embarrassed to explain its loss.

relics.name: Captain Lex's Raid Roster
relics.desc: Every Guild fence and safehouse the Watch suspects, with the night each will be raided.

relics.name: Ayleid Substructure Map
relics.desc: A crumbling chart of the Ayleid passages under the Imperial City, older than the Empire above them.

relics.name: Elder Scroll
relics.desc: Taken from the Imperial Library in the White-Gold Tower. It is impossible to read for long without the world going soft at the edges.

relics.name: Umbranox Family Ring
relics.desc: The ring of the Counts of Anvil, missing for decades. The Gray Fox gave it to me to return.

tgc_gray_fox: The room in the Waterfront hideout is dark except for one lamp. A figure in a grey hood sits behind it, and his face slides out of memory as soon as you see it.
Armand speaks well of you. I need someone who can go where I can't, and do it without leaving bodies for the Watch to count.
This cowl was stolen from Nocturnal herself, long ago. It hides who I am from the whole world. Including the people I love. I mean to be rid of it.
tgc_scroll_read: The Gray Fox unrolls the Elder Scroll. Light that is not quite light pours over his hands, and for a moment the hideout seems to remember a different past.
There. It's done. The world will remember a man named Corvus Umbranox, Count of Anvil. He didn't vanish. He only went away for a while.
And the cowl stays with the Guild. Someone has to wear it. I think it should be you.
tgc_homecoming: This ring. I would know it anywhere. Where did you... no. He's home. He's in the courtyard, isn't he? I can feel it.
Millona Umbranox crosses the hall without another word. Through the window, two figures meet beside the fountain and do not let go.

quests.title: Tryouts on the Waterfront
quests.offer: I hear there's a guild down here that isn't on any charter.
quests.pitch: Could be. Could be it's a story the Watch tells to justify its budget. If you want to find out, take something that isn't yours in this city, and lift a purse without anyone feeling it go. Then come back and we'll talk like friends.
quests.desc: Armand Christophe, the doyen of the Thieves Guild on the Imperial City Waterfront, will let me try out for the Guild. I need to steal something and pick a pocket without getting caught.

objectives.text: Steal two things without being caught
Pick someone's pocket
Return to Armand Christophe on the Waterfront
objectives.reply: Light enough. Rules, then: we don't kill, we don't steal from the poor, and we don't steal from each other. Break any of those and the Gray Fox will hear of it. Welcome to the Guild.

quests.outro: I passed Armand Christophe's tryouts and joined the Thieves Guild of Cyrodiil, which answers to the Gray Fox.

quests.title: The Magistrate's Ring
quests.desc: Word came through the Waterfront that S'krivva, the Guild's doyen in Bravil, has a job for a fresh pair of hands: a magistrate who fines beggars for sleeping in the rain has a gold ring she'd like to see change owners.

objectives.text: Travel to Bravil
Speak with S'krivva
objectives.reply: Yes. The magistrate keeps his seal ring in a box by his bed, because he trusts no one. He is right not to. His house is on the north side, beside the canal. Bring the ring, and touch no one.

objectives.text: Steal the magistrate's ring from his house
Bring the ring to S'krivva
objectives.reply: Good. Now he will have to beg for a new seal, and the clerks will make him wait a very long time. This one is pleased. The fence pays well for gold like this.

quests.outro: I stole a Bravil magistrate's seal ring for S'krivva. The beggars of Bravil, I'm told, had a very good week.

quests.title: The Watch Captain's List
quests.pitch: It should. Captain Hieronymus Lex of the Watch has decided the Gray Fox is a personal insult. He's planning raids on our fences and safehouses, and he keeps the list in his office. Get that list, warn S'krivva, and get out of the city before he locks the gates.
quests.desc: Captain Hieronymus Lex of the Imperial Watch is planning raids on the Guild's fences. Armand Christophe wants me to steal Lex's raid roster from the Watch office and warn the Guild before the gates close.

objectives.text: Steal the raid roster from the Watch office
objectives.journal: Lex's office was tidy to the point of obsession. The roster lay squared to the edge of his desk, with a dagger laid across it as a paperweight.

objectives.text: Slip out of the Imperial City before the Watch seals the gates
Bring the roster to S'krivva in Bravil
objectives.topic: Lex's raid list. Every fence he knows about.
objectives.reply: Then he will find empty rooms and cold hearths. Our people move tonight. This one will see Armand hears of this, and the Gray Fox after him.

objectives.text: Lie low while the raids come up empty

quests.outro: Lex's raids found nothing but empty rooms. The Guild knows who to thank, and so, I suspect, does the Gray Fox.

quests.title: The Gray Cowl
quests.desc: The Gray Fox himself has asked to meet me in the Waterfront hideout. He wants help with a theft that has never been attempted: an Elder Scroll from the Imperial Library, and a way in that the Palace guard knows nothing about.

objectives.text: Meet the Gray Fox
objectives.reply: I did. The Elder Scrolls can rewrite what the world remembers. With one, I can be free of this cowl's curse. The way in is under the city, through Ayleid halls older than the Tower they hold up.

objectives.text: Find a way into the Imperial Substructure
Get past the old guardians of the substructure
Recover the map of the Ayleid passages
Bring the map to the Gray Fox
objectives.topic: The passages run right under the White-Gold Tower.
objectives.reply: Better than I hoped. Rest tonight. Tomorrow we steal from the Emperor himself, and no one is going to get hurt doing it.

quests.outro: The Gray Fox showed me his face, briefly, and told me about the cowl. Beneath the Imperial City there is a road into the White-Gold Tower, and I have the map.

quests.title: Theft of the Elder Scroll
quests.desc: With the Ayleid map, I am to climb from the Imperial Substructure into the White-Gold Tower and steal an Elder Scroll from the Imperial Library, without killing anyone.

objectives.text: Enter the deep passages of the substructure
Deal with what waits in the deep passages
Steal the Elder Scroll from the White-Gold Tower
objectives.journal: I came up through a seam in the floor of the Library, under the noses of the Palace guard. Nobody saw me. Nobody bled.

objectives.text: Bring the Elder Scroll to the Gray Fox
objectives.topic: The Scroll. And no one saw me take it.
objectives.reply: No one ever will, either. Stand back. I've waited a long time for this.

quests.outro: I stole an Elder Scroll from the White-Gold Tower. The Gray Fox read it, and the world remembered his true name: Corvus Umbranox, the lost Count of Anvil.

quests.title: The Count of Anvil
quests.desc: Corvus Umbranox is going home to Anvil and to the wife who waited for him. Before he goes, he asked me to carry his family ring to Countess Millona, and to take up the Gray Cowl after him.

objectives.text: Travel to Anvil
Give the Umbranox ring to Countess Millona
objectives.topic: Countess. Someone asked me to return this to you.
objectives.reply: Thank you. Whoever you are. Thank you.

objectives.text: Return to Armand Christophe
objectives.topic: The Gray Fox is gone home. He left me the cowl.
objectives.reply: Then the Gray Fox isn't gone at all, is he? Don't tell me your name. I'll forget it anyway. Welcome back, Fox.

quests.outro: Corvus Umbranox is home in Anvil. I wear the Gray Cowl now, and the Thieves Guild of Cyrodiil answers to the Gray Fox, as it always has.
